name: me.borders/borders
title: Borders
description: How long the wait is at border crossings and airport passport control, now and by the hour.

tools.name: search_border_crossings
tools.description: Use this when the person names a border crossing, a town at a border, two countries or an airport and you need its id. Not for crossings around a place: use list_border_crossings_near. Answers border crossings and airports' passport control whose names, towns or countries match the words in any order, any language Borders knows, plurals, case or a typo: each with its id, its names, the two countries or the airport's city, and its link on borders.me; the closest names when nothing matches; at most 50.

tools.name: list_border_crossings_near
tools.description: Use this when the person asks what crossings are around a place or around them. Not for which one to take: use find_best_crossing. Answers the border crossings and airports nearest a town or crossing named in near, or lat and lon, each with its distance in km and its car lane's wait now; at most 20.

near.description: a town or a crossing: Lviv, Medyka, Tijuana

tools.name: get_border_wait
tools.description: Use this when the person asks how long the wait or the line is at a crossing or an airport now. Not for another hour or day: use get_usual_wait. Answers one crossing or airport now: each direction, and in it every lane (cars, trucks, coaches, walking, NEXUS, SENTRI, Ready Lane, FAST, or the airport's passport control) with its wait, where the number comes from, when it was read and whether it is older than its source usually is; the usual for this hour beside it.

crossing.description: a crossing's or airport's id as search_border_crossings shows it, or its name (Medyka, San Ysidro, Peace Bridge)

tools.name: get_usual_wait
tools.description: Use this when the person asks when to cross, which hour or day is quiet, or how long it usually takes. Not for the wait right now: use get_border_wait. Answers a crossing's usual wait by hour, Monday to Sunday, for one direction and lane (the car lane by default), from the past weeks' counts, with the shortest hours named and tonight's shortest; or one day's hours when day is given.

crossing.description: a crossing's or airport's id as search_border_crossings shows it, or its name (Medyka, San Ysidro, Peace Bridge)

direction.description: the country the lane goes into: Poland, Ukraine, the United States

lane.description: cars (the default), trucks, coaches, walking, NEXUS, SENTRI, Ready Lane, FAST

tools.name: find_time_to_leave
tools.description: Use this when the person must be across a border by a time and asks when to get in line. through_by is a time in their words (16:00, 4 pm tomorrow). Not for the wait now: use get_border_wait. Answers the latest time to join the line to be through by the time given, at today's pace and the usual for those hours, with how sure it is; in the crossing's time zone.

crossing.description: a crossing's or airport's id as search_border_crossings shows it, or its name (Medyka, San Ysidro, Peace Bridge)

through_by.description: a time in the person's words: 16:00, 4 pm tomorrow, Saturday 9:00

direction.description: the country the lane goes into: Poland, Ukraine, the United States

lane.description: cars (the default), trucks, coaches, walking, NEXUS, SENTRI, Ready Lane, FAST

tools.name: find_best_crossing
tools.description: Use this when the person asks which border crossing to take from where they are or will be. into is the country they are going to. Not for one crossing's lanes: use get_border_wait. Answers the crossings into the country named, from a town or lat and lon, ranked by the drive to each (Apple Maps) plus its wait now, each with the drive, the wait and the total.

into.description: the country they are going to: Ukraine, Poland, Canada

lane.description: cars (the default), trucks, coaches, walking, NEXUS, SENTRI, Ready Lane, FAST

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to tell Borders something: a wrong wait, a missing crossing, an idea. Only their words, never include the conversation. Not for questions about a wait: answer from the other tools.
